name: Brandes et al. 2023 against ProteinGym clinical on ESM-1b and EVE: developer reply on the Supplementary Table 2 values
description: Review of discrepancy-36711e250f9269de, revision 3: explained, developer reply recorded.

attributes.rationale: The explanation in revision 2 stands: Brandes et al. 2023 rank by global ROC-AUC across all variants and ProteinGym's clinical benchmark averages AUC per gene, and the developers' own Methods say EVE is ahead on the gene-average ROC-AUC. This revision records a developer reply about the Brandes values the finding rests on. Rewire asked on ntranoslab/esm-variants issue 16 why the Results text gives ESM1b against EVE as ROC-AUC 0.905 against 0.885 on 36,537 ClinVar variants and 0.897 against 0.882 on 30,497 HGMD/gnomAD variants, where the EVE row of Supplementary Table 2 gives 0.906 against 0.885 on 36,522 and 0.898 against 0.884 on 30,483. A developer of ESM1b replied that the two came from code that was meant to be identical but differed slightly, and recommended the Supplementary Table 2 values. The finding's Brandes results are the Supplementary Table 2 values, so none of them changes, and ESM1b is ahead of EVE in the text and in the table alike. The reply does not concern global against per-gene AUC. The four text values stay recorded as printed with status disputed; whether to supersede or annotate them is a separate record change.
attributes.upstream_response: Reply by nadavbra on 2026-10-22 (https://github.com/ntranoslab/esm-variants/issues/16#issuecomment-6331908966). On ESM1b against EVE: the code behind the main text and Fig. 2b (36,537 ClinVar and 30,497 HGMD/gnomAD variants) was meant to be identical to the code behind Supplementary Table 2 and Fig. 2e-h (36,522 and 30,483 variants) but had minor differences, for example "a handful of protein sequences mapped differently"; the ROC-AUC difference is at most 0.002. "I recommend taking the numbers from Supplementary Table 2, which reflect the released version of the benchmark". On stop-gains: "The Methods counts (32,441 NMD and 36,113 pathogenic overall) are the ones used in the analysis." The difference from the Fig. 6d legend and Supplementary Methods counts (32,362 and 36,034) is probably 79 pathogenic variants whose stop codon falls at the 50 bp boundary, grouped with the NMD variants but left out of those counts; excluding them moves ESM1b's NMD ROC-AUC from 0.5658 to 0.5664. The Table_of_results_stop_gains values are ROC-AUCs over the whole set, and Fig. 6d plots means over 20 bootstrap draws. The issue is closed.
